title: Selected sector average hourly earnings rise through August 2026 while sector levels remain distinct
source_unit: BLS Current Employment Statistics average hourly earnings of all employees, selected private industries

denominator.unit: available monthly seasonally adjusted CES observations

average_hourly_earnings_ytd.unit: US dollars per hour, arithmetic mean of January–August monthly values

monthly_values.unit: US dollars per hour, January through August

observations.method: Arithmetic mean of eight BLS seasonally adjusted monthly average-hourly-earnings observations retrieved from the official CES series page.
observations.uncertainty: July and August are preliminary and the series can be revised; CES is an establishment average, not a worker-level wage trajectory, and does not observe hours, benefits, job quality, control, or bargaining.
observations.subgroup: All employees in manufacturing establishments; no worker demographic or occupation subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: Average pay can rise while worker purchasing power, hours, employment security, or discretion do not improve; composition and establishment mix can affect the aggregate.

observations.counterinterpretation: A high sector average does not identify who receives the pay, how pay varies within firms, or whether a worker has greater outside options or decision rights.

related_sources.claim: The August 2026 Employment Situation release supplies the current publication context and marks August establishment estimates preliminary where applicable.
The latest JOLTS release provides a separate establishment-based mobility context through July 2026.

boundary: This record extends the selected-industry CES earnings context through August 2026 using a partial-year series-page vintage. It does not establish worker-level wage growth, real purchasing power, job quality, bargaining power, household security, or a causal relationship with AI adoption, union membership, or quits. It must not be treated as a complete 2026 annual mean.
